title: Ethiopian Misir Wat with Egg
localName: ምስር ወጥ እንቁላል — Misir Wat be-Inqiilal
community: All of Ethiopia — the egg-enriched lentil stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Misir Wat with Eggs — Misir Wat with whole hard-boiled eggs added and pierced so they absorb the berbere lentil sauce. The egg-enriched version of the most important fasting dish — for fasting days when eggs are permitted.
longDesc: Misir Wat with eggs follows the same logic as Doro Wat with eggs — whole hard-boiled eggs pierced and added to the sauce, absorbing the berbere into their whites and yolks. On fasting days where eggs are permitted (varies by denomination), this version provides complete protein.
ingredients: 4 hard-boiled eggs — pierced all over with a skewer
steps: Make Misir Wat (ETH101) through to completion.
Pierce eggs deeply with a skewer — many holes.
Add eggs to the finished Misir Wat.
The egg whites should have absorbed some berbere colour.
chefTips: Pierce deeply with a skewer — fork holes are not deep enough.
The eggs need only 10—12 minutes — the lentil sauce is already hot.
commonMistakes: Shallow piercing — eggs stay white inside.
sustainabilityTips: Eggs add complete protein to a plant-based dish efficiently.
servedWith: On fasting days when eggs are permitted
storage: Best eaten on day of preparation.
healthBenefits: All essential amino acids from the combination.
culturalNote: Misir Wat with egg bridges the fasting and non-fasting worlds — on the particular fasting days where eggs are permitted, this combination provides the complete protein that sustains the faithful through their observance.
